commitResults.messageBody:
The team plans to replace matches with sessions: activities on a date
that members are assigned to. Upcoming commands such as session add,
assign and view need a Session model to build on, but none exists yet.

Let's add sessions to the model and storage, without any commands or
UI yet, so that those features can be built in parallel.

* Add SessionName, Session and UniqueSessionList. Session names are
  unique ignoring case. Sessions refer to members by email, as emails
  are unique and cannot be edited.
* Add session methods to HobbyHub, Model and ModelManager, and
  getSessionsOf(Member) to find the sessions a member is in.
* Remove a member from every session when the member is deleted, so
  that sessions never refer to a missing member.
* Save sessions in the data file. Files without a sessions list still
  load, and emails that match no member are dropped with a warning.
* Add two sample sessions, and enable assertions for gradle run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match session members by email ignoring case
commitResults.messageBody:
Sessions refer to members by email, but editing a member's email left
their sessions with the old email. Email comparisons in sessions were
also case-sensitive, while members are unique by email ignoring case,
so a session listing ALICE@example.com lost alice@example.com on load.

Let's keep sessions in step with members:

* Replace the old email in every session when a member's email is
  edited.
* Compare emails ignoring case in Session#hasMember and withoutMember.
* When loading, match session emails to members ignoring case and
  store the member's own email.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add member and session list switching
commitResults.messageBody:
Sessions exist in the model, but there is no way to see them, and
commands like add and delete always act on members.

Let's track which list is showing and let commands follow it:

* Add ListState to Model, starting with the member list.
* Let list -m and list -s switch lists. Plain list re-lists the
  current one.
* Parse add, edit, delete and search for the list that is showing.
  The session versions are placeholders that reject the command
  until each is implemented.
* Show a session list panel and a "Members" / "Sessions" heading,
  and swap panels in MainWindow when the list changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify parser routing between member and session lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Each list command chose its parser with a separate ternary, so the
session branches only ran in tests that end in an exception and were
reported as uncovered.

Let's choose the parser in one helper, parseForList, so every case
is a single call. Also test a blank, non-empty session list cell.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh list panel when a command fails
commitResults.messageBody:
A command can switch the list and then fail, e.g. list -m succeeds
in changing the list state but saving the data throws. MainWindow
only refreshed the panel on success, so the session list stayed on
screen while later commands acted on members.

Let's refresh the panel whether or not the command succeeds.

* Move showCurrentList() into a finally block in executeCommand
* Add a regression test that switches lists, then fails to save

Let's add mark and unmark for the session list. * Add Session#withCompleted to copy a session with a new status * Add MarkSessionCommand and its parser for both commands * Route mark and unmark only while the session list is shown * Document both commands in the user guide
